title: Research
text:
Current research directions

PPG signal quality assessment
I work on methods to detect and classify low-quality PPG segments in wearable monitoring. This is important because noisy signals can reduce the reliability of heart rate, pulse rate variability, blood pressure, and other physiological estimates.


Robust peak detection in PPG
I am interested in noise-resilient peak detection methods for PPG signals, especially in wearable and real-world monitoring conditions.


Reproducible biomedical AI
I am interested in biomedical AI methods that are transparent, reproducible, and useful for translational healthcare engineering.

title: Pietro Chierico
text:
I am a PhD student in Biomedical Engineering at Universitat Politècnica de València, affiliated with BioMIT.org, and a visiting researcher at Khalifa University.
My research focuses on digital health, physiological signal processing, wearable sensing, photoplethysmography, cardiovascular monitoring, and AI-driven biomedical technologies.
I am interested in developing reliable and reproducible methods for biomedical signal analysis, with applications in wearable and translational healthcare engineering.
